generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, this means handling sources the same connected way on every essay and report. You use APA, the style psychology expects, cite each source as you write, build a matching reference, and keep the list consistent. The citation in your text and the entry in your reference list are two ends of one thread, held together by APA. Running all three as one practice is what keeps your psychology referencing accurate.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students each write an essay on a theory, each drawing on several studies. Tom treats referencing as separate jobs: he cites as he goes, but throws the reference list together at the end, mixing APA with pasted database entries. Amara runs it as one practice: APA chosen first, every study cited and given a matching reference, and a final check of the whole list. Both read the same studies, but only Amara's referencing holds together under a marker's eye.
generatedProse.summary: Referencing in psychology is most useful when you treat it as one connected practice, not three separate jobs. You run the same parts in order on every essay and report: use APA, cite each study, build a matching reference, and check the list is consistent. Handling all three as one practice is what keeps your psychology referencing accurate.

check.body: A student chooses one style, cites each source as they write by quoting or paraphrasing, builds a matching reference for each, and checks the list is consistent before handing in. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the student is using referencing as one practice: each part connects, from the citation to the reference to the consistent style.
_items.feedback: Yes. Every part is there, connected, working as one practice.

_items.text: That the student is doing far more than any piece of work needs.
_items.feedback: No. Each part does a different job, and together they make the referencing sound.

_items.text: That only the final check at the end really matters.
_items.feedback: Not so. The earlier parts did the real work; the check only confirms it.

_items.text: That citing and building references are the same step.
_items.feedback: They are different parts: you cite as you write, and build the full reference for the list.
